slot.brief: Identify reagents to convert aniline to a target (e.g. benzene via diazonium, or iodobenzene) in correct order.

stem: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of reagents required to convert aniline into benzene?

verdicts.working: Aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273–278 K gives benzenediazonium chloride (diazotization). H3PO2/H2O reduces the diazonium group, replacing N2+ by H to give benzene. Option B (Cu2Cl2/HCl, Sandmeyer) gives chlorobenzene; C (warm H2O) gives phenol; D has the reagents in the wrong order.

working:
The conversion of aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$) to benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$) occurs in two steps:

1. **Diazotisation:**
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 + \text{NaNO}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \xrightarrow{273\text{--}278\text{ K}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

2. **Deamination (Reduction):**
Hypophosphorous acid (phosphinic acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) acts as a mild reducing agent that replaces the diazonium group with hydrogen:
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + \text{N}_2 + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 + \text{HCl}$$

Therefore, the correct sequence is (i) $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl},\ 273\text{--}278\text{ K}$, followed by (ii) $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2,\ \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Independent check: Aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273–278 K gives benzenediazonium chloride (diazotization). H3PO2/H2O reduces the diazonium group, replacing N2+ by H to give benzene. Option B (Cu2Cl2/HCl, Sandmeyer) gives chlorobenzene; C (warm H2O) gives phenol; D has the reagents in the wrong order.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option B: Yields chlorobenzene via the Sandmeyer reaction instead of benzene.
Option C: Yields phenol by hydrolysis of the diazonium salt upon warming with water.
Option D: Reverses the sequence; $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ cannot reduce aniline directly to benzene without forming the diazonium intermediate first.
